entries.title: Generate an SSH key
entries.summary: Creates a private/public key pair used to log in to GitHub without passwords.
entries.when: Once per machine (WSL and Windows each need their own key).

steps.label: Press Enter to accept the default file; set a passphrase (recommended)
Only if ed25519 is unsupported on an old system

entries.warning: If ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 already exists, do not overwrite it - you would lose access anywhere that key is used.
troubleshooting: PowerShell 'ssh-keygen not recognized': enable 'OpenSSH Client' in Windows Optional Features, or use Git Bash.
If asked 'Overwrite (y/n)?' answer n and choose a different filename.

entries.title: Add the key to the SSH agent
entries.summary: Loads your key into memory so you type the passphrase once per session.
entries.when: After generating a key, or when Git asks for the passphrase repeatedly.
entries.where: Linux/WSL: any directory. Windows: an Administrator PowerShell for the first step.

steps.label: Windows step 1: enable and start the agent (once)
Windows step 2: add the key (normal PowerShell)

entries.expected: 'Identity added: ...' then 'ssh-add -l' lists your key fingerprint.
troubleshooting: 'Could not open a connection to your authentication agent': run the eval line first (Linux).
'Error connecting to agent: No such file': start the ssh-agent service (Windows step 1).
Agent is per terminal session on Linux; add 'AddKeysToAgent yes' to ~/.ssh/config to automate.

entries.title: Add your public key to GitHub
entries.summary: Gives GitHub your PUBLIC key so it can recognise you.
entries.where: Terminal for the first step; browser for the rest.

code: 1. Copy the whole line (starts with ssh-ed25519, ends with your email).
2. GitHub > profile picture > Settings > SSH and GPG keys > New SSH key.
3. Give it a title (e.g. "Ubuntu laptop"), paste the key, click Add SSH key.
steps.label: In your browser

entries.warning: Only ever share the .pub file. The file without .pub is secret.
entries.expected: The key appears in your GitHub SSH keys list.
troubleshooting: Never paste the file WITHOUT .pub - that is your private key.

entries.title: Test GitHub SSH authentication
entries.summary: Checks that GitHub accepts your key.
entries.when: After adding the key, or when git push/clone fails.
entries.expected: First time: type 'yes' to trust github.com. Then: "Hi USERNAME! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access."
troubleshooting: Permission denied (publickey): key not in agent (ssh-add -l) or not added to your GitHub account.
Hi <someone else>!: you are using another account's key; use an SSH config with IdentityFile.
Connection timed out on port 22: see 'SSH over port 443'.

entries.title: SSH config: pick a key, or use port 443
entries.summary: A ~/.ssh/config entry that pins your key and works through firewalls that block port 22.
entries.when: Port 22 is blocked, or you have several keys/accounts.
entries.expected: Same success message as the normal SSH test.
troubleshooting: Remove 'AddKeysToAgent' if your OpenSSH is very old and complains about it.
Config indentation is two spaces; no tabs required but be consistent.

entries.title: Fix 'UNPROTECTED PRIVATE KEY FILE' permissions
entries.summary: SSH refuses keys that other users can read.
entries.when: On Linux/WSL when ssh says permissions are too open.
troubleshooting: WSL and Windows have SEPARATE ~/.ssh folders. A key made in PowerShell is not visible inside WSL.
Keys stored on /mnt/c/... cannot be chmod'ed properly; keep keys inside the WSL home folder.
